Quote: "sablefile sync" renders each `[[file]]` template and writes the result to its target. With no flag, sync writes files. Each written file is then recorded in the lock file, `sablefile.lock`. [sec:sync-default]  
Answer: Yes, in sablefile 1.1, if you run sync with no flags, the target files are written straight away. [sec:sync-default]

Quote: "With no flag, sync prints the plan and writes nothing." [sec:sync-default]
Answer: No, the target files are not written when running sync with no flags. [sec:sync-default]

Quote: "A placeholder is a name in double braces, such as `{{project}}`." [sec:placeholders]  
Answer: No, `${project}` is not the right way; the correct syntax is `{{project}}`. [sec:placeholders]

Quote: "Version 2.0 moves the lock file to a new place. The first 2.0 command that reads an older lock file handles it as described in lock-migration." [sec:install-upgrade]  
Answer: No, sablefile 2.0 does not read sablefile.lock in the project root in the same location; it moves the lock file to a new place, and the first 2.0 command that reads an older lock file handles it according to the lock-migration rules. [sec:install-upgrade]

Quote: "sablefile check --no-fail" runs the check as usual and prints each `DRIFT` line. It exits with status 0 even when files have drifted, so a script can report drift without stopping. Without the flag, check exits with status 1 when any file has drifted. The flag changes only the exit status. It does not change which files are reported. [sec:no-fail-flag]
Answer: Yes, use the `--no-fail` flag with `sablefile check` to make it exit with status 0 even when a file has drifted. [sec:no-fail-flag]

Quote: "Version 1.1 adds `**`. It matches zero or more folders, so `docs/**/*.tmp` matches `docs/a.tmp`, `docs/x/a.tmp` and `docs/x/y/a.tmp`." [sec:ignore-recursive]  
Answer: Yes, an ignore entry of `docs/**/*.tmp` will catch a file two folders down, like `docs/x/y/a.tmp`. [sec:ignore-recursive]

Quote: "A leading `!` negates an earlier match, so `!keep.log` brings back a file that an earlier line excluded." [sec:ignore-syntax]  
Answer: Yes, in 2.0, a leading `!` negates an earlier match, so `!keep.log` brings back a file that an earlier line excluded. [sec:ignore-syntax]

Quote: "The lock file is `sablefile.lock` in the project root. It holds one line for each generated file: the SHA-256 hash of the file's content, two spaces, then the path." [sec:lockfile]  
Answer: One line of the 1.0 lock file holds the SHA-256 hash of the file's content, two spaces, then the path. [sec:lockfile]

Quote: "The file has no timestamps, so syncing the same content again produces an identical file." [sec:lockfile]  
Answer: No, syncing the same content twice in 2.0 will produce the same lock file each time. [sec:lockfile]

Quote: "When a fetch of a remote template fails, sablefile retries it up to 5 times before it gives up. The count is fixed in 1.1, and no flag or setting changes it." [sec:remote-retries]
Answer: sablefile retries up to 5 times when a remote template fetch keeps failing, and no flag or setting can change this in 1.1. [sec:remote-retries]

Quote: "Use `--retries N` to set another count; see retries-flag." [sec:retries-flag]  
Answer: Pass `--retries 2` to sync. [sec:retries-flag]

Quote: "The `[values]` table maps names to strings. Each name can be used as a placeholder in a template." [sec:config-values]  
Answer: The `[values]` table in sablefile.toml holds the values a placeholder can name. [sec:config-values]

Quote: "The new file has a `[values]` table with one entry, `project`, set to the folder name, and no `[[file]]` tables." [sec:init-command]  
Answer: A `[values]` table with one entry, `project`, set to the folder name, and no `[[file]]` tables. [sec:init-command]

Quote: "When check finds a drifted file, it prints `DRIFT` and the path, and exits with status 0. Because the status is 0 even when files have drifted, a script cannot detect drift from the exit status in this version." [sec:check-exit-status]

Quote: "When check finds a drifted file, it prints `DRIFT` and the path, and exits with status 1. A check with no drift exits with status 0." [sec:check-exit-status]

Quote: "In 1.0, each entry is a shell glob, such as `*.log`, matched against the target path. A target is ignored when any entry matches it. [sec:ignore-syntax]

Quote: "A line such as `*.log` matches at any depth." [sec:ignore-syntax]  
Answer: Yes, an ignore entry of `*.log` in sablefile 2.0 skips a target at `docs/build.log` because `*.log` matches at any depth [sec:ignore-syntax].
